text: A move writes a new delegation_limit row that carries the next limit_version of the same limit in state PENDING_APPROVAL, and the row in force is changed only at the approval, when it is closed with valid_to and state SUPERSEDED; the decision code, the level, the product group and the conditions of the moved row are copied from the row it moves, because this story's pattern list carries no DP-07 and its contract-dependency list no RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
why: The legacy story and the FSD name the move and no row model, and the table is a version-carrying table of this service, so the change has to be modelled either as an edit of the row in force or as a new row version; an edit would let a limit change before Risk approves it.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.19 and A2.6.4.2; TSD P4 v3 T3.0 (state, version), T3.1 delegation_limit DF-REF-016 to DF-REF-026 and DF-REF-055 to DF-REF-062; Temporal and Drools design (versioned limits, approve-and-date); Architecture v5 slide 14; ownership map ASM-A6-tables-4.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of RWB-P4-E1038-APP
impact: If a move must edit the row in force instead, the approval gate disappears and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP can answer a limit that Risk has not approved.

text: The row a move supersedes carries valid_to as the day before the valid_from of the row that supersedes it, and its state becomes SUPERSEDED in the same transaction as the approval, so exactly one version of a limit is in force on any date.
why: The sources fix that rows stay readable with a valid_to once a new version is approved and name no rule for the closing date of a move, so the day-before rule has to be chosen or two rows would be in force on the effective date.
read: FSD P4 v3 A2.6.4.2 (the rows of DOA-2026.11 stay readable with valid_to 2026-12-31 while DOA-2027.01 is in force from 2027-01-01); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-025 and DF-REF-026; Temporal and Drools design.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the tech lead of rwb-access
impact: A different closing date leaves two rows in force on the day a change takes effect, and the lookup of RWB-P4-E2013-APP would answer the lower level or the higher one depending on the order of the rows.

text: The change event rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 is published on rwb.access.events.v1, keyed by delegationLimitId, with the payload delegationLimitId, limitVersion, decisionCode, approvalLevel, productGroup, effectiveFrom and reason, and with no holder reference, no substitute reference and no personal data.
why: Architecture v5 names the event on the topic and names no payload, so the field list and the exclusion of the person references have to be fixed or the event would either be unusable by a subscriber or publish the delegation table's person references to every consumer.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41 (rwb.access.events.v1: AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 DF-REF-017 to DF-REF-019, DF-REF-023, DF-REF-024 and DF-REF-055; NFR-040; DP-09.
confirm: Risk and model risk officer and the data steward
impact: A payload that carries the holder or the substitute publishes person references to every subscriber; a payload without the version or the effective date cannot be used to refresh a limit cache.
